findings.title: website_name is not properly guarded and can leak restricted website data
findings.body: UserSerializer uses include_<attribute>? methods to decide whether an attribute is serialized. The new method is named include_website_name without the trailing question mark, so it is not used as an inclusion guard. In addition, website_name is derived from website, which is listed in untrusted_attributes, but website_name itself is not treated as untrusted. As a result, a TL0 user's website host/path can be exposed to anonymous viewers even though website is supposed to be hidden. Use include_website_name? and/or add :website_name to untrusted_attributes.

findings.title: Domain comparison can match unrelated hosts and misses some related subdomains
findings.body: The same-domain logic compares raw DNS labels with ends_with? and by stripping the first label, rather than comparing registrable domains. This can treat public suffixes or hosts such as com, co.uk, or shared IP octets as the same domain, showing the full path incorrectly. It also does not handle the reverse subdomain case where the Discourse host is the parent of the website host, for example Discourse at example.com and website at blog.example.com. A proper registrable-domain check or explicit subdomain rules would avoid incorrect display.

findings.title: Spec does not cover website_name visibility for restricted/untrusted users
findings.body: The untrusted_attributes spec list was not updated to include website_name. Since website_name is derived from website and the serializer does not correctly guard it, the current tests will not fail when website_name is leaked for a TL0 user viewed anonymously. Add a test that website_name is absent when website is restricted, and tests for blank/invalid website values.
